newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP sees gas expansion on track.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP sees gas expansion on track.

text.p: The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd said on Thursday that discussions were well advanced on the proposed expansion of the North West Shelf gas project off Western Australia.

The proposal, which hinges on final sales agreements for gas from the North West Shelf from existing Japanese customers, would lift annual output to over 14 million tonnes a year from the current 7.5 million, the project partners have said.
"We see ourselves on track for expansion", said Mike Baugh, president of BHP's petroleum division for Australia and Asia.

Speaking at an industry conference, Baugh also said the Wanea Cossack offshore oil platform on the North West Shelf was producing at a rate of about 100,000 barrels of oil per day (BPD). Wanea Cossack has been plagued by weather and technical problems since it was commissioned in 1995 and was recently said by one of the partners to be producing about 90,000 bpd.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf are BHP and units of The British Petroleum Co Plc, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside Petroleum Ltd, and Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp.

Baugh said domestic exploration by BHP would focus more on North Australia in the near term but over time would decline on a national level. "Expenditure in Australia is coming down ... and basically we see it as a mature area," Baugh said. At the same time exploration in other regions such as the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic would gain importance, he said.
